messages:
Maya Li: Heads-up — we need to finalize trace retention/TTL policy for spans. Prod costs are spiking and queries for week-old traces are slow. Thinking env-based TTL + hot/cold split. Anyone object?

Alex Chen: +1 to env-based. Suggest hot = 7d for prod, 2d for staging, 12h for dev. Cold into S3/BigQuery for 90–365d depending on compliance.

Priya Gupta: How will signaled traces (alerts/bugs) be promoted to hot? We don’t want to lose traces tied to active incidents.

Samir Patel: We can add a retention override on trace attributes: if span has tag `x-retain=high` or if trace matches incident id, copy to hot store. Simple rule engine in pipeline.

Dmitri Volkov: We should define cost limits first. Current estimate: keeping 30d hot for prod ≈ +48% infra bill. Need quantifiable SLOs for trace query latency to justify.

Maya Li: Agreed on costs. Proposal: default hot TTL by env (prod 7d, staging 3d, dev 12h). Promote to hot on: 1) explicit `retain=true` tag, 2) traced error rate > 5% over 5m, 3) attached incident. Cold TTL: archive to S3 for 1y with 30d delayed transfer.

Alex Chen: That sounds reasonable. Also consider aggregated traces (rollups) kept in hot longer — store span histograms / service-latency aggregates for 90d in hot to speed common queries.

Priya Gupta: Implementation detail: OTLP exporter -> collector -> pipeline processors. We can add a `retention` processor that sets metadata and routes to two exporters (hot and cold). Example config: 
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
processors:
  retention_selector:
    rules:
      - env: production
        hot_ttl_days: 7
      - env: staging
        hot_ttl_days: 3
exporters:
  hot_storage:
    endpoint: https://traces-hot.internal
  cold_storage:
    endpoint: s3://redwood-trace-archive
service:
  pipelines:
    traces: [otlp, retention_selector, hot_storage, cold_storage]
```

Samir Patel: Nice. We should also add a sampler before exporters to control ingress volume. Probabilistic baseline + dynamic sampling for high-error traces.

Dmitri Volkov: On querying: cold-only reads will be slower. UX in Console should surface where traces live and offer one-click retrieve (warm restore) for a trace from cold. Otherwise users will open tickets constantly.

Maya Li: Good call — add a restore workflow: Console shows "Archived" with a <restore> button that copies trace to hot for 24h and notifies callers. We’ll need RBAC and rate-limit restores.

infra-bot: cost-dashboard update: prod-hot-storage-monthly = $18,400; cold-archive-monthly = $2,300 (est).

Priya Gupta: Two operational questions: 1) How do we enforce TTL (hard delete vs mark-and-gc)? 2) How do we handle cross-env traces (customers using prod + staging correlation ids)?

Alex Chen: Enforce via GC jobs that delete expired spans from hot indexes. Cold archive retention enforced by S3 lifecycle rules. For cross-env traces, tag origin env and keep correlation metadata in cold so we can rehydrate full trace if needed.

Samir Patel: One more: backups of cold storage metadata (trace index) need to be queryable. Maybe keep compact index in BigQuery for ad-hoc queries across archive without full restore. That'll cut restore frequency.

Dmitri Volkov: Agree. Compact index: one row per trace with service list, time range, error flag, env, and S3 pointer. Keep index for 1y in BigQuery.

Maya Li: Next steps: Priya to draft retention policy doc with TTL table + promo rules. Alex to prototype retention_selector in collector and show perf impact. Samir to sketch restore flow UX and rate limits. Dmitri to run cost/latency model. Meet Friday sync to sign off.

Priya Gupta: I'll start the doc and tag owners. Quick Q: Should we allow teams to override hot TTL per project?

Alex Chen: Allow with guardrails (budget cap + approval). Self-serve with audit logs.

Maya Li: +1. Need audit trail in Console. Also add telemetry metric `trace.restore.count` and `trace.hot.size_bytes`.

infra-bot: Planned meeting created: #retention-policy-sync Friday 11:00 — invites sent.

Samir Patel: Thanks — will bring a simple PoC.

Dmitri Volkov: I'll run numbers and post in the meeting thread.

Maya Li: Thanks everyone — closing for now.
